name: CagriSema
lead: CagriSema is an investigational once-weekly injectable combination of cagrilintide, an amylin-receptor agonist, and semaglutide, a GLP-1 receptor agonist, developed by Novo Nordisk for weight management and type 2 diabetes. [1][4][38] The appearance connection runs through fat loss: reduced appetite leads to lower body weight, which people pursue for a leaner body and face. It is not an appearance product in itself and is studied in adults with overweight or obesity, with or without type 2 diabetes. [1][7]

In the 68-week phase 3a REDEFINE 1 trial in adults without diabetes, the combination produced a mean body-weight change of about 20 percent versus about 3 percent with placebo, ahead of semaglutide alone (about 15 percent) and cagrilintide alone (about 12 percent), according to Wikipedia's summary of the trial. [7][38] A meta-analysis of three early randomized trials found greater weight loss than semaglutide 2.4 mg alone, with more gastrointestinal adverse events. [4] In an open-label head-to-head trial reported by the developer, it did not meet the non-inferiority endpoint against tirzepatide. [1]

Per Grokipedia, Novo Nordisk filed a new drug application with the US FDA in December 2025, and the product was not approved anywhere at the time of that source; a European filing and a 2027 launch were described as planned. [1] Online, CagriSema is mentioned alongside other newer peptides such as retatrutide, mostly as a coming successor to semaglutide. [15]
infobox: Amylin receptor agonist + GLP-1 receptor agonist (fixed combination)

paras: The studied use is chronic weight management in adults with obesity, or with overweight plus a weight-related condition, with or without type 2 diabetes [1][7][8]. Separate phase 3 programs have also examined its effects on blood glucose in type 2 diabetes and on blood pressure [10][11][12]. Registered trials include studies in adolescents with type 2 diabetes, people with hypertension and obesity, and weight-loss maintenance [16][17][18].

Developer-reported programmes beyond weight loss include REDEFINE 3, a cardiovascular outcomes trial that Grokipedia describes as ongoing, and a paediatric programme. [1] Cagrilintide alone has also been tested: Wikipedia reports a 2021 phase 2 dose-finding trial in The Lancet and, in REDEFINE 1, a mean 11.8 percent weight reduction with cagrilintide versus 2.3 percent with placebo. [40]

A phase 2 trial in type 2 diabetes tested the coadministration of cagrilintide 2.4 mg and semaglutide 2.4 mg against each agent alone [9]. In the 68-week phase 3a REDEFINE 1 trial in adults with overweight or obesity, CagriSema was compared with placebo and with each component alone [7]. Wikipedia lists results of -20.4% for CagriSema, -14.9% for semaglutide, -11.5% for cagrilintide and -3.0% for placebo among 3,417 participants, and Grokipedia reports about 80% of participants with gastrointestinal adverse events [38][1]. The companion trial in adults with overweight or obesity and type 2 diabetes (REDEFINE 2, 1,206 participants) reported smaller reductions: Wikipedia gives -13.7% versus -3.1% with placebo and Grokipedia gives 15.7% versus 3.1%, figures that appear to reflect different analysis conventions [8][38][1]. A blood-pressure analysis of REDEFINE 1 has also been published [11].

A 2024 meta-analysis of three randomized trials with 430 participants reported a mean difference of about -9 percentage points in weight versus semaglutide 2.4 mg at 20-32 weeks, with high heterogeneity; gastrointestinal events and vomiting were higher with the combination [4]. Phase 3 REIMAGINE trials in type 2 diabetes have been published in 2026 [10][12]. Recent network meta-analyses and reviews place CagriSema among next-generation obesity drugs expected to achieve weight loss in the range of tirzepatide [2][3][5][6][13].

In the REDEFINE 4 open-label head-to-head trial against tirzepatide 15 mg, as reported by Grokipedia, weight loss was 20.2% to 23.0% with CagriSema versus 23.6% to 25.5% with tirzepatide, and non-inferiority was not met [1]. Ongoing registered trials include a 2,500-person phase 3 study and a trial of switching from semaglutide [19][20].

A phase 2 programme preceded phase 3: Wikipedia reports average weight loss of 15.6 percent after 32 weeks in the earlier trial, with HbA1c improving more than with cagrilintide alone. [38] REDEFINE 5, a phase 3a trial in 331 participants in Japan and Taiwan, reported -18.4 percent with CagriSema versus -11.7 percent with semaglutide, according to Wikipedia. [38]

Network meta-analyses and reviews generally place CagriSema among next-generation obesity drugs, with weight loss expected near the range of tirzepatide. [2][3][13] A 2026 Guardian headline cited by Wikipedia described the drug as "obsolete" in the context of newer agents, though the article's content was not reviewed here. [38]

The reported adverse-event profile resembles that of the GLP-1 class: nausea, vomiting, diarrhea and constipation, mostly mild to moderate [1][4]. Grokipedia reports about 6% discontinuation for adverse events and injection-site reactions in about 12% of users [1]. Since the product is unapproved, no official label or contraindication list exists.

The semaglutide component carries the class boxed warning on thyroid C-cell tumours seen in rodents and a contraindication in people with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN 2, according to Wikipedia's semaglutide article; common effects of semaglutide are nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, constipation and abdominal pain, peaking during dose escalation, with gallstones and rare gastroparesis also reported. [39] Grokipedia lists acute pancreatitis and gallbladder disorders among serious risks noted for CagriSema. [1]

Semaglutide activates GLP-1 receptors and cagrilintide acts on amylin receptors; amylin is a hormone co-secreted with insulin that influences satiety and postprandial glucose [14][6]. Reviews describe combining hormones with complementary actions as a strategy to increase weight loss beyond GLP-1 agonism alone [3][5]. Grokipedia reports a 16-week dose-escalation period [1].
Wikipedia describes cagrilintide as a long-acting amylin analogue (also called GLXC-26801) and describes it elsewhere as a dual amylin and calcitonin receptor agonist. [40][38]

Because CagriSema is unapproved, any use outside trials would involve unregulated product. Posts in a T Nation thread group it with retatrutide and other research peptides that users describe positively. [15] Regulators have not authorised it for sale. [1]

The market context is semaglutide's commercial history. Wikipedia reports that Ozempic was approved by the FDA in December 2017 and Wegovy in June 2021, that shortages were declared from August 2022, that the Novo chief executive said up to 1.5 million Americans were using compounded GLP-1 products as of January 2026, and that counterfeit Ozempic pens were reported in Europe in October 2023. [39] Grokipedia says no price had been announced for CagriSema and cites one analyst estimate of up to $9.61 billion in US sales by 2037. [1]

Phase 2 results of cagrilintide plus semaglutide in type 2 diabetes published in The Lancet; CagriSema enters phase 3. [9][38]

lore.intro: CagriSema appears only briefly in community discussion, usually as an upcoming or research-grade successor to semaglutide, listed beside retatrutide. [15]

claims.claim: CagriSema "kicks ass" for fat loss alongside retatrutide
claims.believers: A forum poster lists CagriSema with retatrutide among compounds they rate highly [15].
claims.experts: Phase 3 trials report roughly 20% weight loss at 68 weeks in adults without diabetes, and published reviews expect weight loss comparable to tirzepatide, though it was reported as not non-inferior to tirzepatide in one open-label trial [7][5][1].

claims.claim: Adding an amylin analogue produces more fat loss than semaglutide alone.
claims.believers: Proponents of combination incretin-plus-amylin therapy argue the two hormones act through complementary appetite pathways. [3][5]
claims.experts: REDEFINE 1 reported about 20% versus about 15% for semaglutide alone, and a meta-analysis found greater weight loss with more gastrointestinal events. [38][4]

claims.claim: CagriSema will match or surpass tirzepatide.
claims.believers: Early phase 2 results were described as comparable to tirzepatide and reviews expected similar weight loss. [38][2]
claims.experts: In the open-label REDEFINE 4 trial against tirzepatide 15 mg, as reported by Grokipedia, non-inferiority was not met (about 23.0% vs 25.5%). [1]

claims.claim: Weight loss from these drugs also costs muscle.
claims.believers: Physique-focused users discuss lean-mass loss alongside fat loss on GLP-1 drugs.
claims.experts: Wikipedia's semaglutide article notes lean mass loss in some studies, with the lean-to-total ratio rising in those studies; CagriSema-specific body-composition data are not summarised.[39]

claims.claim: Research-peptide versions of new weight-loss drugs are interchangeable with the real product.
claims.believers: Forum users group CagriSema with research peptides they rate highly. [15]
claims.experts: Wikipedia reports counterfeit semaglutide pens and FDA warnings on compounded salt forms, and CagriSema itself has no approved supply. [39][1]

card.summary: Not-yet-approved weekly semaglutide plus cagrilintide shot that cut weight about 20% in phase 3 trials.
card.note: Investigational; unapproved supply is unregulated. GI side effects common.

quick.overview:
CagriSema is a once-weekly injection that pairs semaglutide with cagrilintide, an amylin analogue. It is being developed by Novo Nordisk for obesity and type 2 diabetes.

Phase 3 trials report about 20% mean weight loss over 68 weeks in adults without diabetes, more than semaglutide alone but less than tirzepatide in one head-to-head comparison.
quick.mechanism: Semaglutide activates GLP-1 receptors and cagrilintide activates amylin receptors; both reduce appetite and slow eating, through partly different pathways.
quick.risks: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea and constipation are the most reported effects, and were more frequent than with semaglutide alone. It is an investigational drug without an approved label; any supply outside trials is unregulated.

chain: Weekly injection activates GLP-1 and amylin receptors
angle.text: CagriSema's studied effect is sustained weight reduction of around a fifth of body weight in trial participants, and people interested in it are generally seeking the leaner physique that fat loss produces. Reviews of semaglutide-class drugs note that some of the weight lost can be lean mass, which is relevant to how the physique ends up looking. [39]
